interpretation.diagram_classification: cosmological / computistic diagram (annus diagram combining the seasons, the qualities and the cardinal directions)
interpretation.interpretation: The diagram shows the year ("ANNUS") at the centre of a large circle, surrounded by overlapping arcs that link the four seasons (AESTAS, HIEMPS, and presumably the two others) with the elemental qualities (CALIDUS, HUMIDUS, FRIGIDUS, SICCA) and with the cardinal directions (UER ORIENS for east, OCCIDENS for west, SEPTENTRIO for north, and presumably a southern term on the right). The interlocking arcs mark the pairs of qualities shared by neighbouring seasons: for example, warm and moist for spring, warm and dry for summer, dry and cold for autumn, and cold and moist for winter. The diagram thus presents the year as a closed cycle in which time, the qualities of the elements and space are ordered together in a single scheme, in the tradition of medieval natural philosophy and computus, as in the Isidorian tradition of the "De natura rerum" with its diagrams of the seasons.
interpretation.evidence: The central label "AN NUS" names the year as the subject. The legible labels are the qualities HUMIDUS, CALIDUS, FRIGIDUS and SICCA, the season names AESTAS and HIEMPS, and the directional terms UER ORIENS, SEPTENTRIO and OCCIDENS, all placed around the ring. The coloured arcs overlap in a lens-like pattern, joining adjacent labels. Several Step 1 readings are uncertain or incomplete. The text at the right (entry 9, probably a season name such as AUTUMNUS) and the lower texts (entries 13-15, possibly a season name and a direction such as MERIDIES) could not be read. Entries 3 and 5 both give CALIDUS, and entry 15 gives a second SICCA; these may be misreadings. The assignment of each quality to a season is therefore inferred from the usual scheme and not fully confirmed by the text. The Step 1 arc entries record only a link to the outer circle and do not capture how the arcs join one another, so the pairing of qualities is partly an inference from the overall layout. The Isidorian attribution is moderately confident and is not shown by any visible text.
